report.summary: The one failing test, test_book_can_be_updated, is a bad assertion in the test itself. It sends year=2001 in the PUT but expects 2002 back, while the app stores and returns exactly what was sent. Fix the test by changing the expected year to 2001 (or sending 2002); no product change is needed.

causes.title: Test expects year 2002 after updating to 2001
causes.explanation: The test PUTs year=2001 and then asserts the stored book has year 2002. The app's update handler writes the submitted year unchanged to the database and returns it, so the GET correctly returns 2001. The expected value in the assertion is wrong, which looks like a typo or a stale expectation. Nothing in the app adds or alters years.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:23: updated = api.update_book(book["id"], title="Final title", author="Someone", year=2001)
app/main.py:215-218: UPDATE books SET title = ?, author = ?, year = ? ... then returns {"id": book_id, **book.model_dump()}
Failure output: {'year': 2001} != {'year': 2002}; status_code assertion on line 25 passed, so the PUT succeeded and only the stored value differs.
search for 2002|2001 finds no other references, so no shared fixture or app logic sets year to 2002.
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py line 27, change "year": 2002 to "year": 2001 so it matches the value sent on line 23.
